name: Eli Ramirez
signout: Eight-month-old admitted with bronchiolitis. He finally fell asleep. He was around 90% on room air earlier; the floor team thinks he may just need time.
correctDiagnosis: Bronchiolitis with hypoxemia and evolving respiratory distress
diagnosisChoices: Bronchiolitis with hypoxemia and evolving respiratory distress

onset.parent: Congestion started three days ago; breathing worsened today.
onset.nurse: Work of breathing has increased during the evening.

feeding.parent: He is taking about half his bottles.
feeding.nurse: Oral intake is reduced and urine output is borderline.

apnea.parent: No pauses or blue spells that I saw.

findings.default: Tired but arousable infant who tracks briefly and then settles.
findings.deteriorating: Fatigued infant with reduced interaction and persistent tachypnea.
findings.postTreatment: Arousable infant with improved interaction and less fatigue.

findings.default: Moderate subcostal retractions with diffuse crackles and intermittent wheeze.
findings.deteriorating: Marked retractions with reduced aeration and persistent hypoxemia.
findings.postTreatment: Retractions are milder with improved aeration; diffuse crackles remain.

findings.default: Mucous membranes are mildly dry; capillary refill is about 2 seconds.
findings.deteriorating: Mucous membranes are dry with reduced urine output.
findings.postTreatment: Mucous membranes are moist and perfusion is normalizing.

orders.name: Nasal suction and repositioning
orders.result: Secretions are removed; aeration and saturation improve modestly.

orders.name: High-flow nasal cannula escalation
orders.result: Work of breathing and oxygenation begin to improve.

orders.name: Bronchodilator trial
orders.result: No sustained improvement in work of breathing.

orders.name: Systemic corticosteroid
orders.result: No immediate clinical change is observed.
